_note: Synthetic reference notes for the dry run. Not market data.

industrial services.view: Recurring maintenance contracts make up most revenue and hold up through cycles. Margins depend on technician utilization and pricing pass-through. Buy-and-build is the common value-creation plan.

risks.mitigant: Contract renewals staggered over five years.

questions: Break out revenue by contract type and renewal date.
Provide technician headcount and utilization by region.

healthcare IT.view: Revenue cycle and clinical workflow software sells on multi-year subscriptions with high retention. Reimbursement policy changes are the main external risk. Lenders favor recurring revenue over EBITDA in this sector.

risks.risk: Reimbursement rule changes reduce customer budgets.
Data-security incident at a hospital customer.
Recurring-revenue loan structure leaves little equity cushion.
risks.mitigant: Conversion to EBITDA covenants by year three.

questions: Provide gross and net revenue retention for the last eight quarters.
List the last three security audits and findings.

logistics real estate.view: Last-mile and bulk warehouses near population centers have run high occupancy with rent growth slowing from peak. Value depends on mark-to-market of in-place rents and cap-rate movement.

risks.mitigant: Underwrite exit at entry cap rate plus 50bps.

questions: Provide rent roll with mark-to-market by asset.

digital infrastructure.view: Fiber and data-center assets sell on long contracts with inflation escalators. Power availability now limits new data-center supply. Capex intensity is high in the build phase.

risks.risk: Power interconnection delays push out revenue.

questions: Provide status of every power interconnection request.
Provide the build budget with contingencies.
